newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear workers strike N.C. tire plant.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear workers strike N.C. tire plant.

text.p: A strike by Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co workers spread Tuesday to a tenth plant even as the giant tiremaker and union representatives continued talking.

About 2,100 workers at a plant operated by Goodyear's Kelly-Springfield subsidiary in Fayetteville, N.C., went out on strike Tuesday, said the company and the United Steelworkers of America, which represents nearly 13,000 Goodyear workers who have been on strike since early Sunday.
The Fayetteville workers were in the midst of contract talks separate from those covering the 13,000 strikers at nine other Goodyear-owned plants, said union spokesman Curt Brown.
United Steelworkers Local 959 represents the Fayetteville employees, who had been working without a contract since September 1996, Brown said.
A Goodyear spokesman confirmed the Fayetteville work stoppage. He said talks covering the 13,000 strikers were continuing in Cincinnati.

That group went on strike Sunday after negotiators were unable to reach agreement on a new three-year contract covering workers at nine Goodyear plants in Ohio, Alabama, Nebraska, Kansas, Virginia, Tennessee and Wisconsin.

From Fayetteville, Goodyear spokesman Richard Evans issued the following statement: "We believe the strike called by the United Steelworkers of America Local 959 is in violation of the collective bargaining agreement between the company and the union. The Kelly-Springfield Tire Corp's Fayetteville plant will be requesting a temporary restraining order to end the work stoppage."
He noted that the Fayetteville plant is not part of the Goodyear master contract negotiations under way in Cincinnati.
The union's Brown said the Fayettevile local was likely negotiating a contract along lines similar to the master contract.
